yearsToFirstCrop.notes: No locally qualified numeric first-crop age was established in the checked primary sources. Record planting date, nursery starting age and propagation method.

yearsToFullBearing.notes: No measured local numeric full-bearing age was established. No yield ramp is inferred.

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: No qualified mature per-plant food kg with age, product basis and management context was established. Missing output remains unknown rather than zero.

chillUnits.notes: No universal numeric chilling requirement is assigned. Check the actual cultivar and site's winter conditions.

pollination.notes: Check the actual cultivar's pollen needs; no universal classification is inferred from a named cultivar.

supplementaryReferences.title: Exact fruit identity and variability
supplementaryReferences.quote: The colour of the fruit does not identify the mulberry species.
supplementaryReferences.doc: Orwa et al. (2009), World Agroforestry, Morus nigra profile
supplementaryReferences.note: The institutional species reference distinguishes fruiting forms and variable breeding systems. Ripe fruits are used as food; a black-fruited tree must not silently inherit this identity or the legal status of another Morus species.

supplementaryReferences.title: South African taxonomic cultivation record
supplementaryReferences.note: The museum lists M. nigra as cultivated in southern Africa and distinguishes naturalised Morus taxa. It gives no ripe-harvest months or quantified yield.

supplementaryReferences.title: Fruit maturity and water context
supplementaryReferences.quote: the fruit are likely to drop before being fully ripened
supplementaryReferences.doc: Orwa et al. (2009), World Agroforestry, Morus nigra profile
supplementaryReferences.note: Institutional management reference links dry roots to early fruit drop. It contains a non-local 15-year substantial-bearing statement; that is not a South African first-crop age and is not used as a forecast.

care: Confirm the exact mulberry species and that the chosen plant is a fruiting form. Fruit colour alone cannot identify it.
Watch water stress during fruit development and record the actual ripe picking months.
purchase: Ask for identified Morus nigra fruiting material with a locally observed season. Do not use a generic black-fruited mulberry or fruitless ornamental as proof of this product.
